headline: FSSAI Expands Water Checks Following Bisleri Unsafe Sample Finding
seoTitle: FSSAI Expands Packaged Water Testing After Bisleri Concerns
metaDescription: Indian food regulators are widening testing to all packaged water brands after a Bisleri sample failed safety tests; the company maintains its safety.
aiSummaryBullets: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) is initiating nationwide tests across all packaged water brands.
The move follows legal action against Bisleri International regarding a single water sample from a September 2025 batch that allegedly exceeded bromate limits.
Bisleri stated that five out of six samples from the facility met standards and disputes the regulator's findings, noting it has not received an official notice.
aiContextParagraph: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has launched a broader investigation into packaged drinking water standards across the country. This regulatory action follows the prosecution of Bisleri International over an allegedly unsafe water sample collected from the company's Goa manufacturing facility in September 2025. According to regulators, the sample failed to meet prescribed safety limits for bromate, a substance that can be carcinogenic. In response, Bisleri asserted that its products remain safe for consumption. The company stated that internal and independent tests of the specific batch showed results within acceptable limits and highlighted that five of six samples collected by authorities during that period were compliant. As the regulator extends testing to other brands, the case highlights ongoing concerns regarding drinking water safety in a market where bottled water is a staple for both residents and tourists.
whyItIsViral: The story is highly viral, covered by six independent outlets with high velocity due to the brand's national prominence in India.
